description: Machine-readable registry of the 26 architecture tests (docs/testing/architecture-tests.md) plus the canary-purity test. Read by scripts/checks/architecture.mjs, which enforces the activation gate: a test whose activationPhase has been reached without an implementation fails the run.

statusValues.ACTIVE: The guarded structure exists now; the check runs on every invocation and must pass.
statusValues.NOT_APPLICABLE_UNTIL_PHASE_X: The guarded structure does not exist yet. activationPhase names the phase at which the structure arrives; from that phase on, an unimplemented check fails the run.

tests.name: Domain purity
tests.notes: Real target: the FIVE pure packages, and `modules/*/domain/` — which held no TypeScript when this note was written and now holds 88 production files, so the module arm stopped being vacuous when Phase 3 landed and is emphatically not vacuous at Phase 5. The built-in self-test proves the check still bites on every run regardless.

tests.name: Layer direction
tests.notes: Modules held no code when this was written; they now hold 484 production files across domain, application, infrastructure and presentation, so the scan runs against a real tree rather than an empty glob. The self-test seeds a domain->infrastructure import and asserts the check fails on it.

tests.name: Module boundary
tests.notes: Cross-module imports must target public-api.ts only. NOT vacuous: 19 modules publish a public-api.ts and the financial modules import each other through it. The self-test seeds a bypass and asserts failure.

tests.name: No ORM leakage
tests.notes: prisma/@prisma imports allowed only under infrastructure/persistence/ paths. Scans apps, packages, and modules source.

tests.name: Ports declared inward
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2 with the first real adapter (modules/audit/infrastructure). Every adapter-suffixed class (Adapter/Writer/Repository/Provider/Store/Gateway/Client/Publisher/Consumer/Relay/Source/Sink) exported from modules/*/infrastructure must implement an interface declared under that module's application/ports/. Self-test seeds an adapter without a port and asserts failure.

tests.name: No business logic in controllers
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2. Declared complexity budget for *controller* files in apps/*/src and modules/*/presentation: max 8 route-decorator handlers, max 250 lines, and no import of any module's domain/ (directly or via @karar/<module>/domain) — domain access goes through a use case. Self-test seeds a fat controller importing domain and asserts failure on both rules.

tests.name: Money discipline
tests.notes: Monetary positions exist now (shared-kernel Money/Percentage/ExchangeRate, financial-engine zero()). Lexical check: monetary-named fields typed as number, and parseFloat/toFixed, in pure packages and module domain/application source. Type-level enforcement deepens with the engine in Phase 2/6.

tests.name: Event catalogue - published events
tests.notes: The catalogue carries 2 events, so the structural check runs against real entries: the catalogue must parse, every entry must be well-formed, every DomainEvent implementation in code must be catalogued, and a publish call site for an uncatalogued event fails. Consumer-side allowedConsumers enforcement deepens when the bus exists (Phase 2 onward).

tests.name: Tenant scoping
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first tenant-scoped repositories. Principal-scoped tables are derived from the canonical migrations (ENABLE+FORCE and not on rls-allow-list.json) and mapped to Prisma delegates via the schema's @@map; every modules/*/infrastructure/persistence file querying such a delegate must have principal context in reach — withPrincipalContext/withTenant, a transaction-local set_config('app.*', …, true) bind, or an import of a same-module persistence binder that has one (the IdentityPrismaScope pattern). The same check enforces SET LOCAL discipline everywhere: set_config('app.*', …, false) and session-level SET app.* fail. Self-test seeds an unscoped principal-delegate query and a session-scoped bind (and asserts the transaction-local binder shape is NOT flagged). Runtime enforcement is layered: withPrincipalContext fails closed on missing keys, and the adversarial suites (modules/*/__tests__, tests/security) prove the RLS boundary on live PostgreSQL.

tests.name: No direct provider access
tests.notes: Forbidden cloud SDK specifiers, provider URI/resource-name literals (gs://, arn:aws, projects/<id>/...), and provider env-var names, outside infrastructure/providers/ and infrastructure/persistence/.

tests.name: Deterministic domain
tests.notes: Real target: financial-engine and the other pure packages, plus `modules/*/domain/`. Forbids system clock reads and random sources in `modules/*/domain/` and the five pure packages.

tests.name: No jurisdiction branching
tests.notes: Lexical check: conditionals and switches on jurisdiction/country identifiers in `modules/*/{domain,application,presentation}`. Those layers now hold real code, so the scan has a genuine subject and finds no branching rather than finding nothing to look at; the self-test proves it fails on a seeded countryCode comparison. Localization and reference-data exemptions live outside these layers by construction.

tests.name: Sealed containment
tests.activationCriterion: sealed-vault module code exists (Documents + Sealed Vault phase). The static SEALED-content scan is part of this test and activates with it; today no code carries SEALED-marked content to scan.

tests.name: Grant required
tests.activationCriterion: SealedRecordStore and SealAccessGrant types exist; vault transaction isolation is implementable and checkable.

tests.name: Event catalogue - payload rules
tests.notes: Shares the catalogue checker with test 8. The payload-rule constraints (SEALED events identifier-only; HIGHLY_SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL payload requires a declared payloadExemption with owner, reason, reviewer) are enforced against every catalogue entry; with zero entries the constraint set runs against an empty list and the catalogue's shape is still verified.

tests.name: Pure packages
tests.notes: Two tiers, both checked in the manifest AND in the source, because node:fs/node:http are builtins a package.json can never reveal. Tier one, the five pure packages: no runtime dependency except @karar/shared-kernel where documented, and shared-kernel itself none (their import shape is test 1s subject). Tier two, purity-constrained: packages/capability-registry may declare @karar/jurisdiction-policy (JurisdictionId) and nothing else, and every import in its source must be ./relative or one of those two — zero framework, ORM, HTTP, filesystem, or cloud dependency, so any layer can import the registry without dragging infrastructure behind it. devDependencies are allowed. Self-test seeds a framework dependency in the manifest and a node:fs import in the source.

tests.name: Storage access
tests.notes: Object-storage client imports (minio, @google-cloud/storage, @aws-sdk/client-s3) only inside modules/documents/infrastructure/ or infrastructure/providers/. Vacuous today; real scan, self-tested.

tests.name: Approval policy
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3.5 with PolicyPacks and the capability registry. A static repository-level check with three arms, because each alone can hold while the rule is dead: (1) every PolicyPack literal in non-test source is read directly — a pack that CLEARS a capability the capability registry declares disclosureBearing must carry a DECIDED approvalPolicies entry for it, and packs declared outside packages/jurisdiction-policy are inspected too; (2) the MISSING_APPROVAL_POLICY rule must still exist in packages/jurisdiction-policy/src/validation.ts; (3) every non-test caller of validatePack/validatePackSet must pass disclosureBearingCapabilityIds, since the rule only fires for the ids a caller supplies and an omitted option disarms it silently. Disclosure-bearing ids are read statically from packages/capability-registry/src, so a disclosureBearing value that is neither a boolean literal nor an expression naming its ids fails rather than being skipped. The real qa/v1 pack clears nothing, so the repository run is vacuous by design; the self-test seeds synthetic packs (one clearing a disclosure-bearing capability with no entry, one with a PENDING_LEGAL_REVIEW entry, one correct — the negative case), an unarmed call site, and an armed one.

tests.name: Kernel surface
tests.notes: packages/shared-kernel/src/index.ts must export exactly the ten universals: Money, CalendarDay, Currency, Percentage, ExchangeRate, Clock, Result, DomainEvent, TenantId, UserId. Any eleventh export, or a missing one, fails. The tenth (CalendarDay) was admitted by ADR-0027 with Platform Owner approval; the cap is ten and an eleventh requires the same route.

tests.name: Pinning
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first legal-consequence tables; completed in Phase 3.5. All four canonical dimensions (data-model.md section 5) are enforced against the REAL canonical migrations, parsed across the WHOLE history — CREATE TABLE plus later ALTER TABLE additions, so a column or CHECK added by a later migration counts. NOTHING is deferred any more: Phase 3 deferred the policy-pack-version and subject-selection dimensions behind a gate that fired the moment Phase 3.5 arrived, migration 0086 resolved it, and the deferral machinery was removed rather than left as a branch nothing can exercise. Three pin shapes, all verified in the schema and never against prose in the checker: a classic pin (column exists and is NOT NULL); a state-paired pin (a nullable value column bought with a NOT NULL state column, plus the three CHECKs that make the pair honest — a closed vocabulary, a tie between the PINNED state and a non-null value, and a creation-cutoff clause so the historical state is not a permanent exemption); and an explicit non-applicability (a NOT NULL state column CHECK-bound to exactly one value, so no row can claim otherwise). Declared tables: consent_grants, data_protection_role_assignments, subject_policy_selections. A declared table may not leave one of its own pinning-signature columns unmapped, and an undeclared table carrying the signature (any *_at_creation column, operating_entity_id, policy_pack_version, subject_policy_selection_version) fails. Self-test seeds every failure shape plus two compliant shapes as negative cases.

tests.name: RLS coverage
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 3 with the first tenant-scoped tables. Parses every canonical migration (packages/platform/db/migrations/*.sql — the schema of record): each created table is either ENABLE + FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with at least one policy, or carried on packages/platform/db/rls-allow-list.json. All three failure shapes detect: no RLS, enabled-without-policy, and FORCEd-without-enabled (the legacy audit tables own anomaly, RLS-01/RLS-02/P14). A stale allow-list entry naming a table no migration creates also fails. Allow-list entries carry more than filled fields: the reason must state why no tenant or subject predicate fits the table (a category such as platform configuration is not a reason) and the compensating grants must describe actual controls rather than a label, both with minimum lengths — an exemption from the tenant boundary is argued, not declared. Live-database verification of the same facts is db:verify plus the adversarial suites (modules/*/__tests__, tests/security), which probe the policies as karar_app and the owner on real rows. Self-test seeds all three shapes, a stale entry, an empty reason, a reason with no scope clause, and compensating grants that are a label.

tests.name: No declared guard without call site
tests.notes: Activated in Phase 2 with the first guard class (audit's AuditMetadataGuard; config guards count as they land). Every class named *Guard in apps/*/src, packages/*/src, or modules/** must be referenced from non-test code outside its own declaration; tests do not count as call sites. Self-test seeds an unreferenced FooGuard and asserts failure.

tests.name: Resource limits declared
tests.notes: Every real mounted ingestion path declares every bound in the CENTRAL policy (packages/platform/src/ingestion/limits.ts), and every central policy belongs to a real path. Fails in both directions, and fails when the tree contains no real path at all — a resource-limit test that scans nothing passes vacuously, and the phase marker moves only WITH a first real mounted ingestion path. Activated with the CSV upload and parse routes.

tests.name: Lifecycle declarations
tests.notes: Deepened in Phase 2 with the first real schema (audit.audit_events): a module with implementation code must declare the full six-field table (subject relationship, purpose, classification, retention, export treatment, erasure strategy), and six-field tables are validated field by field — canonical subject/classification/erasure values, export treatment included|excluded (reason)|n/a with 'excluded' requiring a stated reason, and placeholders (TBD/TODO/empty) forbidden. Skeleton modules without code keep the erasure-only obligation. Also parses packages/platform/db/DATA_LIFECYCLE.md (platform-owned tables: schema_migrations now; workstream D appends outbox/jobs rows) with the same six-field rules. Self-test seeds a non-canonical strategy, a code-bearing module without the six-field table, and a placeholder row.

tests.name: Assurance-claim traceability
tests.notes: Referential integrity of docs/security/assurance-claims.md: every AC-### row has non-empty evidence and owner; statuses limited to VERIFIED/PENDING/UNVERIFIED; every test N evidence reference exists in this registry; every backticked repository path in an evidence cell resolves on disk; every evidence id is well formed (EV-###, defined once in docs/compliance/evidence-register.md); and this registry contains all 26 canonical tests. Whether the evidence SUPPORTS the claim stays a human review, per section 1 of the registry — this asserts only that the pointer points somewhere real. Self-test seeds an empty evidence cell, a ghost test reference, a path that does not exist, and a malformed evidence id.

tests.name: Canary purity
tests.activationCriterion: The sealed-integrity canary is designed and implemented (key custody strategy phase); its plaintext becomes inspectable for customer-derived content.
